input: Plan a weeknight taco bar for the family

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The number of people and their ages (e.g., young kids vs. adults) directly affects quantities, topping variety, and how hands-on the setup needs to be.
Knowing which proteins and toppings to include vs. exclude — especially dietary restrictions like vegetarian, gluten-free, or allergies — shapes the entire menu.
A tight weeknight time budget (e.g., 30 min vs. 1 hour of active cooking) determines whether shortcuts like rotisserie chicken or pre-shredded cheese are necessary.
Whether this is a regular Tuesday dinner or a special occasion (birthday, end-of-week treat) changes the effort level and presentation expectations.
How the taco bar is physically set up — buffet on the counter, items in slow cookers to stay warm, or plated at the table — affects what equipment and serving vessels are needed.
Flavor preferences (mild vs. spicy, crunchy shells vs. soft tortillas, Tex-Mex vs. street taco style) define the character of the whole meal.
Understanding what 'done well' looks like — minimal dishes, kids eating without complaints, impressive spread — helps prioritize which parts of the plan matter most.

gold.taskTitle: Plan a weeknight taco bar for the family
gold.taskDescription: Organize a casual, self-serve taco bar dinner on a weeknight for the family, covering menu, prep, and serving logistics.

questions.title: How many people are you feeding, and what are their ages?
questions.description: Knowing the headcount and whether there are young kids, teens, or only adults determines portion sizes, topping complexity, and how the bar should be organized.

questions.title: Does anyone have dietary restrictions or strong dislikes?
questions.description: Identifying vegetarian, gluten-free, allergy, or strong preference needs shapes which proteins, shells, and toppings make the menu.

questions.title: How much active cooking time do you have that evening?
questions.description: A 20-minute window calls for very different shortcuts than a relaxed 60-minute prep, affecting whether anything needs to be made ahead or bought pre-made.

questions.title: Is this a regular weeknight dinner or a special occasion?
questions.description: A casual Tuesday dinner versus a mini celebration changes the expected effort, presentation, and whether extras like a themed dessert are worth including.

questions.title: Do you prefer soft tortillas, crunchy shells, or both?
questions.description: Shell style is a defining preference that also signals the overall flavor profile — street taco simplicity versus Tex-Mex crunch — and drives the rest of the topping choices.

questions.title: How do you want the food kept warm and served at the table?
questions.description: Whether you plan to use slow cookers, skillets on trivets, or just serve everything at once affects which equipment to pull out and how the physical bar is arranged.

questions.title: What would make this taco night feel like a win for you?
questions.description: Clarifying the top priority — minimal cleanup, everyone happy at the table, an impressive spread, or quick execution — helps focus the plan on what matters most.
